reason: This passage (Exodus 17:8-15) recounts the battle between Israel and Amalek at Rephidim. The text describes military conflict, Moses's role in supporting Israel through raised hands, and God's recorded speech, which consists of: (1) instructing Moses to write a memorial, (2) declaring God will blot out Amalek's memory from under heaven, and (3) vowing perpetual war against Amalek. There is no complaint from Yahweh about the people. In fact, God actively supports Israel's victory and makes promises of future judgment against Amalek. The narrative presents God as an ally to Israel in this conflict, not as one expressing dissatisfaction with the people.
